rationale: Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical trait/phenotyping (corneal dystrophy), covariates, training cohort/size, ancestry distribution, and validation size, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. The main differentiators are the representative validation metric and structural properties: PGS002042 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384) and is a genome-wide shrinkage score with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is generally favorable for capturing polygenic signal when endpoints and study context are otherwise identical. Therefore PGS002042 has the clearer multi-field advantage over the strongest runner-up (PGS001835).

PGS001135 is the only candidate that is a direct arthritis (EFO: arthritis) model with explicit PRS-comparable performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R2=0.00291, with basic covariates and a heritability-sane R2 well below the provided h2_liability ceiling). The closest runner-up is PGS004547 (same broad arthritis EFO and similar UKB-based context), but it provides no PRS-only AUC/R2 and only a modest per-SD OR (1.26), making its standalone PRS strength less well-supported in the visible record. The other candidates are endpoint-mismatched subtypes (juvenile idiopathic arthritis; psoriatic arthritis) for a generic 'arthritis' target.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, identical training cohort (UKB), training N (391,124), evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS), covariates (age/sex/PCs etc.), and validation sample size (19,864). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either, the only differentiators are structural: PGS002034 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45) and has a trivially higher partial correlation (0.0563 vs 0.0562) with essentially identical CI. Given the same endpoint and study context, the higher-capacity LDpred2 genome-wide score is the better-supported pick over the extremely sparse penalized-regression score.

All candidates are direct matches to major depressive disorder, but PGS002759 has the strongest PRS-specific performance proxy available: an OR per SD of 1.26 (95% CI 1.22–1.30) under basic covariate adjustment (age, sex, PCs, technical covariates), which is cleaner and more interpretable for PRS signal than the others’ small full-model R² values. The closest runner-up is the near-clone PRSice-2 set from the same preprint (PGS003578/PGS003580/PGS003576) with slightly higher reported R² (~0.024–0.026) but these are not labeled PRS-only and thus are less comparable; their differences are also tiny. PGS003333 is an EHR/PheWAS-oriented score with unknown covariates and only a modest Nagelkerke R²=0.022, offering weaker, less clean evidence than PGS002759’s effect-size signal.

PGS002786 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly matches the target (bipolar disorder), whereas PGS002787 and PGS002788 are subtype-specific (bipolar I/II). All three come from the same publication, use the same method (SDPR), have similar EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry and basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes; the only available metric is a small partial R²/full_model_r2 that is not clearly PRS-only and is therefore a weak differentiator. Although PGS002788 has a slightly higher partial R² than PGS002786, the endpoint fidelity signal favors the direct bipolar disorder model over subtype scores given otherwise near-clone metadata.

PGS001263 is the only candidate with an exact atrial flutter endpoint across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, and it provides clean PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.617, PGS R2 no covariates=0.025) under basic covariates, with R2 remaining below the heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0157; scale differences aside, no red-flag inflation). The strongest runner-up is PGS001339, which is very similar (same paper, same covariates, similar validation size) but has a less specific combined AF+flutter time-to-event phenotype and slightly weaker PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.613; R2 0.024). PGS002050 and PGS001841 are also AF+flutter (not flutter-specific) and report only partial-r without PRS-only AUROC/R2, making them less directly comparable despite larger training N.

All candidates map to angina pectoris, but PGS001262 has the strongest directly comparable PRS-only evidence: highest PGS-only AUROC (0.5868) and PGS-only R² (0.0130) among the snpnet UKB siblings, with basic covariates and a larger validation sample (n=49,472) than PGS001261/PGS001260. The MVP PheCode models (PGS005048/PGS005052) are endpoint-faithful and report strong per-SD ORs (~1.49), but they lack PRS-only AUROC/R² and only provide a covariate-adjusted C-index, which is not a substitute for PRS-comparable metrics; their tiny full-model C-index difference vs each other is negligible. Given the shortlist, PGS001262’s combination of endpoint alignment and best PRS-only performance makes it the most supported pick over the closest runner-up PGS001261.

All top candidates are EUR-only and evaluated on incident aortic stenosis, but PGS005254 is the cleanest direct-match disease PRS: trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly aortic stenosis and phenotyping_reported is incident aortic stenosis with only basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs). Versus the strongest runner-up PGS005252, although PGS005252 reports a high full-model C-index (0.87), it uses a much heavier clinical covariate set (multiple comorbidities and BMI/smoking/renal failure), making that discrimination less attributable/comparable to the PRS; PGS005254 avoids this packaging and still shows strong PRS signal via HR=1.64 (1.50–1.78) with larger training (n=205,483). The other siblings (PGS005255/PGS005256) are less endpoint-faithful at the trait label level (valve function measures) and have weaker HR (~1.53), and PGS004911 is for a different disease (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy).

PGS001344 is the strongest direct-match on comparable PRS-only performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.64568 and PGS-only R²=0.05973 (no covariates), which is both cleanly comparable across models and plausible under the asthma liability h² ceiling (~0.1515). The main runner-up is PGS001782, which also reports a covariates-regressed-out (PRS-comparable) Nagelkerke R²=0.048844 but is from a global biobank framework paper and has weaker PRS signal than PGS001344 on the key comparable metric. Other candidates either rely on full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics (PGS002727) or provide non-AUC/R² metrics (partial-r in PGS002061), making them less directly benchmarkable despite large samples.

All candidates are near-clones from the same publication with identical trait/phenotyping (breast cancer / breast carcinoma), same training cohort (UKB), same ancestry setup, same validation size, and no covariates listed, so the main differentiator is within-family performance. PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest reported validation signals among the set: highest full-model AUROC (0.6625 vs 0.6598 for the closest runner-up PGS004040) and highest R² (0.0764 vs 0.0739), plus the largest per-SD effect size (OR 1.826 vs 1.809). Given the near-identical context, these consistent advantages support selecting PGS004153 as the best-supported direct-match candidate.

PGS001267 is the best-supported direct match because it targets the exact ankylosing spondylitis endpoint (phenotyping_reported matches the target) and, unlike most alternatives, reports clean PRS-only discrimination metrics in European validation (PGS-only AUROC=0.7265; PGS-only R²=0.0988) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). The strongest runner-up is PGS001268, which has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R² but is explicitly time-to-event (TTE) in phenotyping_reported, a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic disease-risk target; given the weak-prior ranked order and the preference for non-TTE endpoints when performance is otherwise similar, PGS001267 is preferred. The portability-study scores (PGS002089/PGS001876) provide only partial-r (weaker/comparability-limited evidence) and PGS003420’s higher full-model AUROC is not PRS-only, has unknown covariates, and is based on a small EAS-only validation (n=1,298), making it less reliable for benchmark-leading selection.

PGS004536 is the strongest direct-match on endpoint (ICD-10 J44 mapped to COPD) and comes from a disease-focused COPD model family in the 2024 Commun Biol paper, with a very strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.49), which is a key proxy for PRS discrimination when AUC/R2 are not reported. Its closest sibling runner-up is PGS004466 from the same publication with the same endpoint/ancestry/variant count, but it has a materially weaker OR (1.31), making PGS004536 the better-supported of the two near-clones. The alternative framework-style candidates (PGS001783/PGS001788) do report PRS-comparable R2, but they are from a global portability/meta-analysis framework and their R2 (0.038 and 0.016) does not clearly dominate the strong OR evidence here; PGS001332 is a sparse pan-trait UKB framework score with very weak PRS-only metrics (AUROC~0.54, R2~0.002).

PGS000327 is the cleaner direct-match for autism spectrum disorder: its phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder” (endpoint-fidelity aligned), it comes from a disease-focused ASD GWAS meta-analysis context (Nat Genet; multiple ASD cohorts listed), and it shows stronger predictive signal in the available comparable proxies (OR per SD 1.33 with tight CI; variance explained R²=0.0245). In contrast, PGS002790 has an explicit endpoint mismatch/withdrawn phenotype (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”) despite ASD labels, lacks training sample details, and reports a much smaller partial R² (~0.0055) in a smaller validation set, making it less supported as a direct ASD risk PRS.

PGS004913 is the most endpoint-faithful and disease-focused candidate: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly target alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis, with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and a dedicated cirrhosis-in-heavy-drinkers study context. It also provides PRS-relevant effect evidence (OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4) and an R²=0.029 that is plausible relative to the provided heritability ceiling. The strongest runner-up is PGS000704, which has a larger, genome-wide model and a slightly higher full-model C-index (0.711), but it comes from a broad UKB framework-style paper and reports only time-to-event full-model performance (no PRS-only metrics), making its apparent advantage less directly attributable to the PRS. PGS001777 is also disease-aligned but is a very sparse 3-variant score with unknown covariates and only a full-model AUROC (0.671), so it is less robustly supported than PGS004913.

All candidates are broadly on-target for celiac disease, but PGS000040 has the cleanest direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease) without the HLA-DQ2.5-carrier restriction seen in PGS000041/PGS000042, and it shows the strongest reported discrimination among the disease-focused scores (full-model AUROC 0.90 vs 0.879 for PGS000316 and ~0.72–0.73 for the HLA-carrier-targeted models). The main runner-up is PGS001301 because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.8287; PGS-only R2 0.1422), but it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework with a broader/less specific phenotype label (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), which is a known generalization risk relative to a disease-focused celiac prediction study; thus PGS000040 is the best-supported direct-match overall despite lacking PRS-only metrics.

PGS002755 is the strongest direct-match eczema/atopic dermatitis PRS in the shortlist on structural grounds while keeping endpoint fidelity acceptable: it targets atopic dermatitis (EFO atopic eczema) with an incident AD endpoint and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants, which is typically more predictive for polygenic disease than sparse genome-wide-significant SNP sets. The closest runner-up is PGS004587, which has the same incident AD endpoint and identical evaluation setting (EUR, n=337,910) but is only 23 SNPs and shows a weaker HR (1.153 vs 1.249 high vs low PRS), suggesting less discriminative PRS signal. The other candidates are less suitable: PGS003486/PGS003459 are for paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (treatment/context-specific endpoint mismatch), and PGS001773’s very high full-model AUROC (0.93) comes from a small n=676 cohort with covariates including parental ethnicity and a moderate-to-severe subtype, making it less reliable/transferable for generic atopic eczema risk.

All three candidates are direct Crohn’s disease matches, but PGS004254 has a clear multi-field advantage over the strongest runner-up (PGS001331): it is a disease-focused score (not the pan-trait UKB “813 traits” sparse framework), uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2-auto) with far broader variant coverage (744,682 vs 257), and reports a strong PRS effect size (OR 2.18 per SD, 95% CI 2.05–2.32), which is a strong proxy for discriminative power. Although PGS004254 lacks explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² (only a full-model AUROC=0.72 with basic covariates), the snpnet framework scores’ available PRS-only metrics are modest (PGS-only AUROC ~0.58; PGS-only R² ~0.006–0.007) and come from a known underperforming portability/framework archetype. Between the two snpnet siblings, PGS001331 is slightly better than PGS001330 (non–time-to-event endpoint and marginally higher PRS-only AUROC/R²), but neither has stronger overall evidence than PGS004254’s disease-focused, genome-wide, high-OR package.

PGS002032 and PGS001824 are near-clone direct matches (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, same UKB portability study, same training N, same covariates, same eval context and identical partial-r≈0.0716). In this near-clone setting, structural signals break the tie: PGS002032 uses LDpred2 with genome-wide shrinkage and a much larger variant set (19,768 vs 22), which is generally more likely to capture polygenic signal and transfer better than a very sparse penalized-regression score when empirical performance is otherwise indistinguishable. PGS000924, despite reporting PRS-only AUROC/R2, is from the sparse pan-trait ‘813 traits’ framework and uses a time-to-event composite phenotype including porphyrin metabolism; its extremely high reported R2 (0.218) also conflicts with the provided h2_obs≈0.089 ceiling, making its metric evidence less trustworthy for this target compared with the coherent direct-match portability siblings.

PGS001033 is the only shortlist candidate whose endpoint maps directly to the target trait at the EFO level (trait_efo = blood coagulation disease) and it reports clean PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.634 and PGS R2(no covariates)=0.0578) on a sizable European validation (n=67,425). The top-ranked alternatives (PGS002034, PGS001826) are narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency phenotypes (trait_efo = congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency), and while they are near-clones with similar partial-r (~0.056), they lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 and are evaluated on a smaller validation set (n=19,864). Between those two, PGS002034 is marginally stronger structurally (genome-wide LDpred2 with 32,552 variants vs 45), but that advantage is not enough to outweigh PGS001033’s better target-level phenotype alignment plus explicit PRS-only discrimination metrics.

All candidates are direct matches for basal cell carcinoma with identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), EUR-only ancestry, and the same publication family, so this is a near-clone comparison where small performance differences are legitimate tie-breaks. Among the top-ranked siblings, PGS000454 matches PGS000452 on full-model AUROC (0.632) but has the highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0489 vs 0.0487) and a stronger top-1% vs rest OR (3.79 vs 3.61), while other siblings have slightly lower AUROC/R² (PGS000456/PGS000458) or materially weaker discrimination despite larger UKB training/validation (PGS000453 AUROC 0.611, pseudo-R² 0.0301, top-1% OR 2.8). With no PGS-only AUC/R² available for any candidate, PGS000454 has the best overall within-family performance signals versus the strongest runner-up PGS000452.

PGS002738 is the strongest direct match to the target (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and is supported by a large genome-wide PRS-CS construction (326k variants) trained on major cohorts (MVP, UKB) with a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,900). It also shows the strongest available discrimination proxy in the shortlist via OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (1.54–2.51), exceeding the closest runner-up PGS002739 (OR=1.76) which is additionally constrained to AFR-only evaluation and a much smaller gene-based variant set (858), a structural disadvantage for a polygenic trait. The older PGS000201/PGS000202 are for ‘problematic alcohol use’/AUD criteria count (measurement phenotype rather than dependence diagnosis) and show smaller incremental ΔR² (0.0119 and 0.0046), making them less endpoint-faithful and less compelling than the AUD case-control style evidence in PGS002738.

PGS001174 is the only shortlist candidate with clean PRS-comparable discrimination reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.623 and PGS-only R2=0.028), and its PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to the provided EUR h2_obs ceiling (~0.021–0.029), supporting that the metric is not obviously inflated. It is also a direct match to cholelithiasis (trait_efo=cholelithiasis; phenotyping_reported=TTE cholelithiasis) with basic covariates. The strongest runner-up is PGS004476/PGS004546 (ICD10 K80 exact endpoint), but those Commun Biol ‘risk factor metaPRS’/LDpred2 models provide only per-SD ORs (1.22–1.30) and no AUC/R2, plus unknown covariates, making their expected benchmark ranking less supported from the visible evidence. The portability-paper options (PGS002072/PGS001861) have broader phenotype (includes cholecystitis) and only partial-r (~0.095–0.098) without PRS-only AUC/R2, so they do not clearly beat the explicit PRS-only performance evidence in PGS001174.

PGS002237 is the strongest overall direct-match package: it is explicitly CKD stage ≥3 with a clear phenotyping definition (eGFR <45), very large disease-focused training (UKB; n=279,819), and—critically—shows the strongest per-SD effect size in the shortlist (OR 1.47, CI 1.32–1.65) plus multi-ancestry evaluation coverage. The main runner-up is PGS005090, which reports a much higher full-model AUROC (0.90) but that metric is not PRS-only and is likely covariate-inflated/less comparable; it also lacks training N and is restricted to AFR-only GWAS/EVAL, reducing general benchmark transferability. The AJHG five-biobank method-evaluation scores (PGS004158/PGS004030) have clean covariates but materially weaker discrimination (AUROC ~0.59; OR ~1.38), and PGS005113 lacks comparable AUC/R2 evidence.

All candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm, but PGS003973 has the clearest overall strength among the disease-focused options: it comes from a large multi-cohort AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.1M variants) with basic covariates (age, age^2, sex) and reports strong discrimination in European evaluation (C-index/full-model AUC 0.882, n=7,517). The closest runner-up is its near-clone sibling PGS003972 from the same paper/method/variant count, but it shows materially weaker reported discrimination (AUROC 0.69) and has unknown covariates, making it less compelling within the same study family. Framework/portability scores (PGS001784, PGS002054) are penalized by their study archetype despite having PRS-only R2/partial-r, and the older sparse P+T score PGS000753 (29 variants; OR 1.37) has weaker structural properties and only moderate effect-size evidence.

PGS004621 is the strongest direct match to the target (trait_efo = cirrhosis of liver; phenotyping_reported = Cirrhosis) while also having the most robust modern PRS construction (PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants) and the broadest disease-focused multi-cohort development/validation context (multiple biobanks; EUR eval) with an extremely large reported validation sample size (n=1,153,995). Against the main runner-up PGS000726 (also cirrhosis of liver), PGS000726 is a sparse 12-variant GWS score with no AUC/C-index reported, whereas PGS004621 provides at least some discrimination evidence (full-model AUROC 0.68 with basic covariates) plus a moderate per-SD OR (1.42 vs 1.32). Other candidates (PGS000704, PGS000776, PGS001777) are alcohol-related/alcoholic cirrhosis subtypes or have more endpoint/packaging limitations and do not beat PGS004621’s combination of endpoint fidelity + genome-wide method + multi-cohort support.

All candidates are direct CAD matches, but PGS003725 is the strongest within the top-ranked Nat Med 2023 multi-ancestry LDpred2 family: it has the largest reported effect sizes (HR 1.75; OR 2.14 per SD) versus its closest sibling runner-up PGS003726 (HR 1.73 only) and PGS003727 (HR 1.67), with similarly clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and the same large validation size (n=308,264). Compared to the main non-sibling alternative PGS002244 (Cell Genom 2022 LDpred), PGS003725 shows materially stronger effect-size evidence (OR 2.14 vs 1.64) while retaining broad multi-ancestry evaluation. PGS000018’s high full-model AUROC (0.89) is discounted because it is not PRS-only and comes with much smaller validation (n=3,309) and a prevalent endpoint label, so it is weaker benchmark-transfer evidence than the Nat Med multi-ancestry score family.

All candidates are direct matches for cervical carcinoma with incident cervical cancer endpoints, but PGS003428 is the only clearly disease-focused, modern genome-wide shrinkage PRS (LDpred; ~2.9M variants) from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis study, which is a strong structural and study-archetype signal for external performance. Its PRS effect size is also the strongest in the shortlist (HR per SD 1.33 vs ~1.20–1.22 for PGS000073/PGS000784), supporting better standalone PRS discrimination despite lacking a PRS-only AUC/R2. The main runner-up is PGS000073 (and near-clone PGS000784), which show much higher full-model AUROC (~0.745) but are sparse 10-variant GWAS-hit scores from cross-cancer/risk-factor integration frameworks with heavier covariate packaging (parity, oral contraceptive use, pack-years), making the AUROC less indicative of PRS strength and the PRS itself likely weaker than the genome-wide LDpred model.

PGS005170 is the strongest direct match to the target trait (dementia) with a disease-focused all-cause dementia endpoint (incident all-cause dementia) and a structurally strong multi-score integrative design (ensemble of 24 component PRSs from LDpred2/C+T/PRS-CS) with very large genome-wide variant coverage (1,320,229). It also shows broader transportability evidence via multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR), whereas the closest high-performing runner-up cluster (PGS004281/PGS004284) is UKB-only EUR development/evaluation and reports only covariate-adjusted full-model AUROC (~0.819) that is not PRS-only and is therefore less reliable as a standalone PRS benchmark signal. Compared with older Alzheimer’s-focused scores (PGS000823/PGS000812), PGS005170 is better aligned to all-cause dementia and is supported by a comparable time-to-event effect size (HR 1.25) while avoiding the very sparse SNP-set limitation of those older models.

All candidates are direct matches for dilated cardiomyopathy, but PGS004949 has the strongest PRS-specific performance evidence among the shortlist while maintaining acceptable endpoint alignment. Compared with the top-ranked PGS004862 (same general disease endpoint, EUR eval, basic covariates), PGS004949 reports an explicit univariate (PRS-only) AUC of 0.68 (CI 0.66–0.69) and a PRS delta liability-scale R² of 0.095, whereas PGS004862 only provides full-model AUROC/R² (0.71/0.05) without isolating PRS contribution. Within the 2024-12-16 Nat Genet sibling set, PGS004949 also edges PGS004951 and PGS004947 on PRS-only AUC (0.68 vs 0.67 and 0.66) with similarly strong per-SD OR (~1.91). Although PGS004949 evaluates in MAE rather than EUR, it has a very large evaluation sample (n=326,106) and provides cleaner PRS-only metrics than the earlier HERMES-based scores, making it the best-supported candidate for expected benchmark performance.

All candidates are direct matches for atrial fibrillation, but PGS005168 is heavily packaged with the CHARGE-AF clinical risk calculator (explicitly flagged as a strong negative for standalone PRS comparability), making its very high full-model C-index (0.8718) largely non-informative for PRS quality. Among the remaining disease-focused, PRS-light models, PGS002814 shows the strongest PRS signal proxies in a comparable basic-covariate setting (age/sex/PCs): highest reported per-SD effect size (OR≈1.94) and the only substantial variance-explained metric (Nagelkerke R2=0.14) alongside AUROC=0.74. This gives it a clearer PRS-strength indication than the closest runner-up PGS005313 (AUROC=0.78 but only age/sex and no PRS-only metric; OR=1.82) and older framework-style PGS000016 (PRS-only R2=0.029). Despite the heritability-ceiling caution on R2 scale, PGS002814 has the best combined endpoint fidelity + PRS-strength evidence without risk-calculator leakage.

PGS002304 has the cleanest endpoint fidelity for the target (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Follicular lymphoma”, trait_efo matches) and provides the strongest available discrimination signal in the shortlist (full-model AUROC 0.61, 95% CI 0.59–0.63). The closest runner-up on endpoint label is PGS003455, but it has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported = “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”) and only a weak per-SD OR (1.07, CI crosses 1) with no AUC/R2, making it less supported. The PRSweb candidates (PGS000644/PGS000643) have coherent EUR-only settings and basic covariates, but they are labeled/phenotyped as “Nodular lymphoma” and show materially weaker performance (AUROC ~0.53–0.54, very small pseudo-R²), so they do not outweigh PGS002304’s better trait alignment and higher reported discrimination.

All three candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_efo=Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported=lymphocytic thyroiditis), same publication family, same evaluation ancestry mix, and same validation N, and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2—so small full-model AUROC differences are weak tie-breakers. Between the strongest alternatives, PGS005270 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.639 vs 0.630) but shows a near-null effect size (OR≈1.04 per SD), suggesting weak PRS signal. PGS005271 combines genome-wide PRS-CS construction (~1.09M variants) with a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.55), which is a more informative proxy for standalone PRS discrimination in this no-PRS-only-metrics setting. PGS005272 is weaker on both full-model AUROC (0.605) and effect size than PGS005271.

All three candidates are direct phenotype matches to Dupuytren contracture, but PGS002092 and PGS001880 are near-clone siblings from the same UKB portability study with identical endpoint/covariates/ancestry context. Between those two, PGS002092 has a small but consistent edge in the only reported PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0797 vs 0.0783) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (484,484 vs 2,443), a structural advantage likely to translate to better external performance when other fields are equal. PGS001254 reports clean PRS-only AUROC/R², but it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (813 traits) with extremely few variants (11), which is a known weaker archetype for generalization; its metric availability alone is not enough to outweigh the stronger same-endpoint, same-study-family evidence favoring the LDpred2 genome-wide score.

PGS005097 is the strongest direct heart-failure candidate overall: it matches the target trait exactly (trait_reported/efo = heart failure) and comes from a disease-focused Nat Genet heart-failure genetics study with broad multi-biobank development and a large independent validation (n=40,989) using only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), reducing leakage concerns. The main runner-up is PGS001790, which has a clean PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.006981) and larger EUR validation (n=358,905), but it is from a general “Global Biobank lessons” framework paper (a known weaker archetype for external benchmark performance) and its advantage is primarily metric availability rather than a clearly stronger disease-focused evidence package. The CHF phecode models (PGS005083/PGS005077/PGS005076) have decent per-SD ORs (~1.44–1.46) but are a slightly narrower endpoint (congestive HF phecode) with smaller validation and no PRS-only metrics; among them PGS005083 is marginally best, yet it does not clearly surpass the broader, disease-focused multi-cohort support of PGS005097.

PGS000114 is the only candidate whose endpoint is the broad target trait itself (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all map to juvenile idiopathic arthritis), whereas PGS000324/PGS000325/PGS000326 are subtype-specific JIA scores (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular) and thus are less faithful direct matches for a generic JIA target. All four are from the same disease-focused publication, same method family (SparSNP), same EUR-only dev/eval ancestry, and similarly light covariates (sex, PCs), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2; therefore the very high full-model AUROC for PGS000324 (0.93) is not sufficient to outweigh the broader endpoint mismatch. Compared with the strongest runner-up (PGS000324), PGS000114 trades lower full-model AUROC (0.738) for correct umbrella-phenotype alignment, making it the best-supported direct-match choice for juvenile idiopathic arthritis overall.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical trait/phenotyping (“Disorders of iron metabolism”), identical covariates, training N, and the same multi-ancestry evaluation setup, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. The main differentiators are (i) slightly stronger PRS signal in the selected European validation record (partial-r 0.1355 vs 0.1307) and (ii) more polygenic genome-wide shrinkage construction with many more variants (LDpred2, 6,713 variants) versus a much sparser penalized regression score (654 variants). Given the otherwise matched context, these two advantages make PGS002031 the better-supported direct-match over PGS001823.

PGS004562 is the strongest direct match to the target kidney failure within the shortlist because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo=kidney failure with a coherent ICD-based endpoint (N18 chronic renal failure) and, crucially, it is a multi-score aggregation model (RFDiseasemetaPRS), which domain guidance flags as a structural advantage over single-score constructions when other evidence is similar. Against its closest near-clone runner-up PGS004492 (same publication, same endpoint, same EUR-only dev/eval, same variant count and validation size), PGS004562 shows materially stronger PRS signal via a higher per-SD effect size (OR 1.395 vs 1.171), making it the better-supported sibling. Other candidates have clearer endpoint mismatches for the target (PGS002237 is CKD stage≥3; PGS000708 is diabetic kidney failure; PGS001272 is a pan-trait sparse framework score with weak PGS-only AUROC/R2), so they are less likely to be the top external-benchmark performer for generic kidney failure.

PGS000788 is the strongest direct-match for the target (trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia; phenotyping_reported=Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia) and it is a near-clone of the main runner-up PGS000077 (same endpoint framing, same basic covariates, same EUR evaluation context and very similar 75-variant construction). Within this like-for-like comparison, PGS000788 shows materially stronger performance proxies (higher full-model AUROC 0.738 vs 0.719; higher C-index 0.756 vs 0.735) and a stronger PRS effect size (HR 1.70 vs 1.45), which is a meaningful tie-break when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent for both. The chronic-lymphocytic-leukemia scores (PGS000874/PGS000648/PGS000646) are less faithful to the broader lymphoid leukemia target (CLL-specific and/or family-history-enriched phenotyping for PGS000874) and have smaller/less generalizable validation contexts, so they are not preferred over the incident lymphocytic leukemia models.

All candidates are EUR-only melanoma PRSs without clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on endpoint fidelity plus the strongest available performance proxies. PGS000813 shows the best discrimination signal in the shortlist with a higher reported AUROC (0.77, 0.75–0.79) than the closest runner-up PGS000743 (0.74, 0.71–0.77), and it also reports strong PRS effect evidence (OR per SD 2.12; and OR top 10% vs middle 20% 5.7). Although its phenotyping is restricted to familial cutaneous melanoma in CDKN2A non-carriers (narrower than generic/incident endpoints in PGS000743 and PGS002246/PGS002247), the combination of stronger reported discrimination and explicit effect-size strength provides the clearest support among the available records, while the others either have lower AUROC (~0.69) or lack comparable effect-size evidence.

PGS000639 is the strongest direct-match within the coherent Cancer PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease cluster (PGS000637/638/639/640): all share the same endpoint (phenotyping_reported/trait_reported = Hodgkin’s disease), EUR-only context, and the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), so their full-model metrics and effect sizes are legitimately comparable as near-clones. Within this like-for-like set, PGS000639 has the best reported discrimination and signal (full-model AUROC 0.62 and Nagelkerke R² 0.0276, with the strongest per-SD OR 1.476) versus the closest runner-up PGS000638 (AUROC 0.601, R² 0.0193, OR 1.377). PGS003449 is penalized despite the label match because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly mismatched (Chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and it shows very weak effect size (OR ~1.02) with no usable performance metrics, making it a poor endpoint-fidelity candidate for Hodgkin lymphoma.

All candidates are direct phenotype matches for multiple myeloma (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all aligned; EUR evaluation throughout), and none reports a clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC must be interpreted cautiously. Between the two top-ranked genome-wide-significant-variant scores with the same variant count (23), PGS002281 has substantially stronger validation support (n=2,395 vs n=290 for PGS002306) and provides corroborating PRS signal via an OR (highest vs lowest quintiles) of 3.18 (2.34–4.33) alongside a moderate full-model AUROC (0.644). PGS002306’s higher full-model AUROC (0.69) comes from a much smaller validation set with unknown covariates, making that apparent advantage less reliable. The older PRSweb scores (PGS000652/653/654) show materially weaker discrimination (full-model AUROC ~0.55–0.58; modest per-SD OR ~1.24–1.33), so they are less likely to be the top external performer.

PGS002763 is the strongest direct-match hip osteoarthritis PRS in this shortlist because it has the cleanest endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = Hip osteoarthritis, matching target) and the strongest PRS-discrimination proxy reported (OR per SD 1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.05M variants) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/technical). The main runner-up is PGS002728, which reports a full-model AUROC 0.66 but is phenotyped as total hip replacement (a treatment/proxy endpoint) and uses a sparse 44-variant GWS score; its AUROC is not PRS-only and is less comparable. The newer Commun Biol scores (PGS004478/PGS004548) have coherent ICD-based hip OA endpoints but weaker effect sizes (OR ~1.30 and ~1.22) and unknown covariates, while PGS004882 is an incident/time-to-event framework-style score with modest C-index (0.60) despite huge validation N, so neither has a clear multi-field advantage over PGS002763.

PGS004908 is the strongest direct-match package in this shortlist: it targets kidney cancer/renal carcinoma with coherent phenotyping (“Kidney cancer”), comes from a large disease-focused multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet), and shows the strongest available PRS signal proxy via effect size (OR per SD 1.50, 95% CI 1.43–1.58). While all candidates lack clean PGS-only AUC/R2, PGS004908 also has the highest reported discrimination among the comparable full-model AUROCs (0.74 vs 0.722 for PGS000076/PGS000787), and its larger variant set (107 vs 19/15) is a supportive structural advantage within the GWAS-hits family. The closest runner-up is PGS000076 (and near-clone PGS000787), which has similar endpoint (incident kidney cancer) and large validation, but weaker effect size (HR ~1.16) and slightly lower AUROC; PGS000787’s additional R²=0.366 appears to be full-model/non-PRS-comparable and is not credible as PRS-only given the very low heritability ceiling provided, so it does not outweigh PGS004908’s stronger disease-GWAS and effect-size evidence.

PGS004236 is the strongest direct-match because it comes from a disease-focused, multi-cohort, explicitly multi-ethnic hypertension study (Nat Commun 2023) with broad evaluation ancestries and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=2.1, 95% CI 1.99–2.21), supporting substantial PRS discrimination even though only full-model AUROC is shown. The closest runner-up is its near-clone sibling PGS004234 from the same paper with essentially identical endpoint/covariates/validation, but PGS004236 has a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.764 vs 0.763) and, more importantly, provides the strong OR evidence while PGS004234 reports no effect size. Framework-style UKB-only scores (PGS001320, PGS004934) have cleaner PRS-only metrics or decent full-model AUROC, but they are pan-trait/portability archetypes and/or have weaker effect-size evidence (e.g., OR 1.42 for PGS004934) and narrower evaluation context, making them less reliable as the top external-performance pick versus the disease-focused multi-ethnic score.

All five candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (myocardial infarction PheCode 411.2; same trait_efo/phenotyping), covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), training cohort (MVP), ancestry framing, and validation size (n=30,379), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2—so selection falls to within-family performance/effect-size differences. PGS005039 has the strongest combined empirical signals among the shortlist: the highest reported full-model C-index/AUC (0.78484 vs next-best 0.78385 for PGS005045) and the largest per-SD OR (1.578, CI 1.50–1.67) compared with the closest runner-up PGS005045 (OR 1.554) and other ldpred siblings (e.g., PGS005035 OR 1.541). Given identical design context, these small but consistent advantages make PGS005039 the best-supported direct-match pick.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical endpoint framing (trait/phenotyping: Tobacco use disorder; EFO: nicotine dependence), same training cohort/size (UKB, n=391,124), similar basic covariates, and same validation sample size (n=19,400), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. The main differentiators are (i) stronger PRS-comparable performance proxy: PGS002037 has higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741 vs 0.0557 for PGS001830) in the selected European validation, and (ii) more genome-wide shrinkage/coverage (LDpred2 with 847,691 variants vs penalized regression with 13,838 variants). Given identical phenotype and study context, the higher partial-r is the clearest empirical edge, supported by the broader genome-wide model.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; EFO Nasal Cavity Polyp), publication, ancestry (EUR dev/eval), training cohort (UKB), training N (174,489) and validation N (56,192), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 or full-model metrics. With metrics absent, the strongest differentiator is the available effect-size signal: PGS004535 reports a materially stronger per-SD OR (1.60) than PGS004465 (1.35), indicating stronger discriminative power in the same study/endpoint context. Although PGS004465 uses LDpred2, the empirical tie-break within the same publication family favors the sibling with stronger observed effect size, so PGS004535 is best-supported.

All candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all gout), come from the same publication, have the same training cohort (UKB), identical stated covariates (0), and the same validation sample size/ancestry context, so the best tie-break is within-family performance. PGS004160 has the strongest reported discrimination and effect size in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.6936 and R² 0.0893; OR per SD 2.05) versus the strongest runner-up PGS004047 (AUROC 0.6851, R² 0.0801; OR 2.00). With no PGS-only AUC/R² available for any candidate, these consistent within-study full-model metrics and OR differences are the most direct comparative evidence, favoring PGS004160.

PGS004614 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused diverticular disease score in the shortlist: it is explicitly for diverticular disease (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported align) and comes from a dedicated diverticular disease GWAS paper, using a genome-wide shrinkage method (SBayesR) with very large variant coverage (~1.08M) and some multi-ancestry evaluation presence. The main runner-up is PGS000997, which has clean PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.591, PGS R2 0.0178) but is from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework (813 traits) and uses a time-to-event endpoint, both of which are weaker external-benchmark signals than a disease-focused genome-wide score; its PRS-only R2 is also only modest and near the trait’s heritability ceiling range, suggesting limited headroom. PGS004544/PGS004474 lack comparable AUC/R2 and appear to be part of a risk-factor integration study with only moderate per-SD ORs (~1.31–1.32), offering less direct evidence than the disease-focused PGS004614 despite PGS004614’s full-model AUROC being covariate-influenced (includes family history).

PGS000328 is the strongest direct systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) candidate in the shortlist: trait_reported/trait_efo are exact for SLE and it shows the highest reported discrimination signal among the disease-focused SLE models (full-model AUROC 0.83) with a larger validation sample (n=1,001) than the closest runner-up PGS000196 (full-model AUROC 0.79; n=245). While PGS000328’s phenotyping is restricted to early-onset SLE (<20), the alternative high-training-size portability-framework scores (PGS001870/PGS002082) target broader ‘lupus’ but only report very small partial correlations (~0.02) and are from a UKB portability sweep rather than a disease-focused SLE study; PGS000754 has much lower AUROC (0.65) despite large validation. Given the lack of any PRS-only AUC/R2 across all candidates, the best-supported choice is the disease-focused SLE score with the strongest available performance proxy versus the nearest comparable SLE competitor.

PGS004911 and PGS004910 are near-clone siblings from the same 2025 Nat Genet HCM evaluation study with identical endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), ancestry (EUR GWAS/EVAL), covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10), cohorts, and similar variant counts. In this like-for-like context, PGS004911 has clearly stronger reported performance proxies than the strongest runner-up PGS004910 (higher full-model AUROC 0.80 vs 0.73; higher R² 0.048 vs 0.031; slightly stronger HR 2.34 vs 1.97 and OR per SD 1.33 vs 1.26; and OR high-vs-median tertile 5.9 vs 5.5). Compared with older alternatives, PGS000739’s higher AUROC (0.821) is confounded by heavy clinical covariates (multiple comorbid risk factors plus rare-variant carrier status), making it less comparable as a standalone PRS, while PGS000778 has a mismatched restricted endpoint and tiny validation (n=368). Therefore PGS004911 is the best-supported direct-match candidate.

All candidates are direct matches for multiple sclerosis by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. The strongest head-to-head is PGS002726 vs PGS000809 because both are disease-focused MS studies with EUR evaluation and report discrimination. PGS002726 shows higher reported AUROC (0.80, CI 0.76–0.82) and a very strong risk gradient (OR top 10% vs median = 15.0, CI 10.4–24.0), which is compelling PRS signal even though the AUROC is a full-model metric and covariates are unknown. PGS000809 has lower AUROC (0.765) and modest R² (0.069) but these are also not explicitly PRS-only, so they don’t provide a cleaner comparable advantage. The UKB portability-framework scores (PGS002038/PGS001831) have only weak partial-r (~0.037–0.040) and are penalized as framework-derived relative to disease-focused MS-specific models. PGS004699 is tied to an optic neuritis presentation context and has lower AUROC (0.752), making it less directly representative of generic MS susceptibility PRS performance despite huge validation N.

PGS004606 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused AMD score in the shortlist: it targets age-related macular degeneration with coherent phenotyping_reported (AMD), uses a genome-wide PRS-CS model (~1.0M variants), and shows strong PRS signal via OR per SD 1.76 (tight CI), with evaluation in Europeans on a large validation sample (n=163,011) and only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). The main runner-up is PGS004952, which reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.842) but is based on only 52 genome-wide significant SNPs, has much weaker effect size (OR 1.41), a much smaller validation (n=1,232), and its AUROC is full-model (not PRS-only) so it is not a clean advantage. PGS004607 is from the same Nat Genet family but has lower AUROC (0.65) and weaker OR (1.48) with GWAS ancestry AFR-only, making it less supported than PGS004606. The UKB framework/portability scores (PGS001013, PGS002041) have weaker/less informative PRS metrics and less disease-focused endpoint support.

All top three candidates (PGS005262/PGS005263/PGS005261) are direct endpoint matches for the target (benign nodular goiter) and come from the same disease-focused multi-biobank study with the same evaluation setting (MAE 100%, n=94,651; same selected validation ancestries). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any candidate, the best differentiators are within-family performance/effect-size signals and method/structure. PGS005262 has the strongest reported evidence among the near-clone siblings: highest full-model AUROC (0.5933 vs 0.5876 and 0.5854) and the largest per-SD effect size (OR 1.41 vs 1.36 and 1.05), while also using genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) rather than the much sparser P+T model (PGS005261). The UKB portability scores (PGS001814/PGS002022) are a weaker study archetype and are also a partial phenotype mismatch (nontoxic multinodular goiter) with only small partial-r (~0.024–0.028), so they do not beat the disease-focused benign nodular goiter cluster.

PGS000053 is the strongest direct-match overall: it targets the exact trait (late-onset Alzheimer’s disease) with a coherent disease endpoint (familial LOAD) and uses only basic covariates (age, sex), avoiding obvious clinical-risk packaging. It also provides a PRS-relevant effect size (OR per SD 1.29, 95% CI 1.21–1.37) with a reasonable EUR validation sample (n=4,792). The closest runner-up is PGS000054 from the same publication family and same 21-variant GWAS-hits construction, but it is evaluated only in AMR/Hispanic ancestry (less aligned to the EUR-centric evidence base here) despite a higher OR (1.73), making it a less reliable default pick for general benchmark performance. Other candidates are weaker due to endpoint/metric concerns: PGS000334 reports a high R²=0.191 that appears to be a full-model/unclear metric and is suspiciously high relative to the provided heritability ceiling; PGS004918 has a small evaluation (n=136) and only a full-model AUROC; PGS002289’s phenotyping is cognition-by-age interaction rather than AD case-control.

PGS001792 is the strongest direct-match on glaucoma/primary open-angle glaucoma with the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence in the shortlist: it reports a covariates-regressed-out PRS metric (PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.03209) alongside AUROC=0.777, and its PRS-only R2 is plausible under the provided glaucoma heritability ceiling guidance. The main runner-up is PGS004944, which has a large evaluation sample and a strong OR (1.74), but its reported AUROC=0.748 is full-model only and the endpoint is self-reported POAG, making its discrimination less directly attributable to the PRS. Other candidates either rely on full-model AUROC with family history included (PGS000137), provide only an OR without comparable AUC/R2 (PGS002761), or come from a portability framework with only partial-r reported (PGS002043).

PGS002767 is the strongest direct-match overall: it has exact endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Knee osteoarthritis”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (~1.05M), and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.30–1.40) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), avoiding heavier clinical covariate packaging. The closest runner-up is PGS002729, which is disease-focused but uses only 24 genome-wide significant variants and reports only a full-model AUROC=0.66 with BMI included (not PRS-only), plus its phenotyping_reported is broader (“Clinical osteoarthritis”) rather than knee-specific. The other alternatives are weaker: PGS001192 is a pan-trait UKB framework TTE score with low PRS-only AUROC (0.5566) and low PGS R2 (0.0068), and PGS004549/PGS004479 have knee-code endpoints but lack performance metrics and have unknown covariates, making them less well-supported than PGS002767.

PGS005265 is the strongest direct-match for the target hyperthyroidism because it targets Graves’ disease (the dominant clinical cause of hyperthyroidism) in a disease-focused, multi-biobank setting with large multi-ancestry evaluation (n=94,651) and shows the best performance/effect-size signals within its near-clone family. Versus the closest runner-up PGS005266 (same study, endpoint, method, and validation context), PGS005265 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.6652 vs 0.6637) and a materially stronger per-SD OR (1.63 vs 1.54), supporting better discrimination. The UKB framework alternatives (PGS001043/PGS001042) report clean PGS-only AUROC/R2, but come from the pan-trait sparse snpnet ‘813 traits’ archetype that typically transfers worse than disease-focused multi-cohort scores; their modest PGS-only R2 (~0.022–0.024) is also well below the trait heritability ceiling and does not clearly outweigh the multi-cohort Graves-focused evidence. PGS005264 is weaker than the PRS-CS siblings (lower AUROC and near-null OR), so it is not competitive.

PGS000078 and PGS000789 are near-clones: same 109-variant Graff et al score, same EUR-only evaluation, same incident lung cancer endpoint, identical covariate bundle (including family history, PM2.5, detailed smoking terms), and essentially identical full-model AUROC/C-index. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any candidate, the small HR difference (1.16 vs 1.17) and PGS000789’s reported R²=0.799 are not interpretable as PRS-comparable and likely reflect covariate-heavy modeling; thus they do not clearly beat the upstream #1. PGS004860 shows higher full-model AUROC (0.893) and uses a genome-wide LDpred2 score, but it is supported by a single smaller case-control cohort (n=24,012) with different covariates and no PRS-only metrics, making the AUROC advantage non-comparable and potentially covariate-driven. PGS000740 is endpoint-shifted to early-onset (<50) and PGS000721 has much lower AUROC and tiny validation. Therefore the best-supported direct-match remains PGS000078.

PGS002766 is the best-supported direct-match for generic hypothyroidism risk because it keeps a clean disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Hypothyroidism) with only basic demographic/PC-style covariates and provides a strong PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.47, tight CI) in a straightforward UKB setting. The main runner-up is PGS005218, which is disease-focused and very large, but its reported AUROC=0.859 is a full-model metric built with heavy near-outcome thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), making that performance largely non-comparable to standalone PRS quality; it also targets incident hypothyroidism specifically. Compared with the older UKB framework scores (PGS000965/PGS001181), PGS002766 avoids the pan-trait sparse-model archetype penalty while still showing comparable discriminative signal via OR.

Both candidates are direct matches to otosclerosis in trait_efo, but PGS001255 provides clean PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.6319; PGS R2 no covariates=0.01341) on a European validation record, whereas PGS002046 reports only a small partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182) and no PRS-comparable AUC/R2. Although PGS002046 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many variants, its lack of PRS-only discrimination metrics makes it harder to justify over PGS001255’s explicit PRS-only AUC/R2 evidence; PGS001255’s PRS-only R2 is also plausible relative to the provided h2_obs ceiling. The time-to-event phenotyping in PGS001255 is a mild endpoint penalty, but not enough to outweigh the clearer PRS-only performance evidence versus the portability-style partial-r-only reporting in PGS002046.

PGS001273 is the cleanest direct match to the generic target trait “osteoporosis” (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both Osteoporosis) and it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.5685; PGS-only R2=0.00688) under basic covariates, staying well below the heritability ceiling (sanity-consistent). The strongest runner-up is PGS001274, which has slightly better PRS-only performance (AUROC=0.57595; R2=0.00945) and more variants, but its endpoint is explicitly time-to-event ‘osteoporosis without pathological fracture’, a narrower/horizon-style framing than the generic osteoporosis target. The other candidates (PGS002768/PGS004565/PGS004560) lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and provide only modest per-SD ORs (~1.31–1.33), so they have weaker comparable performance evidence despite larger variant counts in the metaPRS models.

PGS003586 is the strongest direct match: it targets pre-eclampsia (trait_reported and trait_efo both align) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping (Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia) in a disease-focused multi-cohort Nat Med study, using the same PRS-CS framework and basic covariates as its sibling. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any candidate, the best differentiator is effect size within comparable design: PGS003586 shows a stronger per-SD association (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.24–1.38) than the closest runner-up PGS003587 (OR 1.20, 1.14–1.26) under essentially identical validation context (EUR, n=25,582). PGS004593 has weaker endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is gestational hypertension despite preeclampsia label) and a smaller effect size (HR 1.16), so its larger validation sample does not outweigh the phenotype mismatch and weaker signal.

PGS001312 is the strongest direct-match on comparable PRS-only performance: it reports clean PGS-only AUROC=0.6916 and PGS-only R²=0.0523 for psoriasis with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a standard psoriasis endpoint. The closest runner-up is its near-clone sibling PGS001313, but that is time-to-event phenotyping (TTE psoriasis) and has materially weaker PRS-only metrics (AUROC=0.6729, R²=0.0497). The other candidates (PGS002083, PGS001871) come from a portability framework and only report partial correlation (~0.063) without PRS-only AUROC/R², making them less directly benchmark-comparable here, while PGS002293 is an incident/lifestyle-packaged GWAS-hits score without PRS discrimination metrics.

PGS005235 is the strongest direct-match obesity candidate on the visible evidence: it has clear endpoint fidelity via a direct obesity phecode (278.1) despite the broader trait_reported label (“Adiposity”), uses only basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and shows the strongest discriminative effect-size signal (OR≈1.97 per SD) among the shortlist—well above the moderate ORs in the closest EUR alternatives. The main runner-up is PGS004447 (EUR, E66 obesity, LDpred2, similar variant scale), but it has weaker effect size (OR≈1.36) and unknown covariates; PGS004517 is even weaker (OR≈1.23) and appears to be a risk-factor metaPRS packaging variant from the same paper family. The EAS-evaluated scores (PGS005154/PGS005145) are endpoint-aligned but are less comparable for general obesity benchmarking here and provide only beta effect sizes without clearer PRS-only metrics. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for any candidate, the materially stronger OR plus clean covariate/endpoint framing makes PGS005235 the best-supported pick.

PGS000903 is the strongest direct-match disease PRS in the shortlist: it targets Parkinson’s disease with coherent phenotype fields, comes from the large disease-focused Lancet Neurology GWAS meta-analysis, uses a substantially richer C+T score (1805 variants) than the sibling GWAS-hit score PGS000902 (90 variants), and shows stronger validation signals in the same setting (full-model AUROC 0.692 vs 0.651; plus a large risk gradient OR(top 25% vs bottom 25%)=6.25). The main alternative with higher AUROC (PGS001774, AUROC 0.80) is heavily covariate-packaged (includes family history and multiple established risk factors), making its discrimination largely non-comparable to PRS performance; other candidates (PGS003763/PGS000123) lack comparable discrimination metrics and are sparse GWAS-hit constructions.

PGS000083 is the best-supported direct match for the broad target “pancreatic carcinoma” because it targets pancreatic cancer mapped to exocrine pancreatic carcinoma with an incident pancreatic cancer endpoint, and it is evaluated in a very large European validation sample (n=391,491) with supportive PRS effect size (HR=1.49 per SD, 95% CI 1.36–1.62). The strongest runner-up is PGS000794, which is essentially a near-clone of PGS000083 (same endpoint, covariates, validation size, and nearly identical AUROC/C-index/HR) but is explicitly described as using inverse variant weights, offering no clear multi-field advantage and potentially adding avoidable implementation risk. PGS002264 reports a much higher AUROC (0.83) but it is a packaged clinical model integrating diabetes-related variables/clinical risk and has unspecified evaluation ancestry plus a narrower PDAC subtype endpoint, making its discrimination less attributable to the PRS and less comparable for selecting a standalone PRS.

PGS005217 is the strongest direct-match for peripheral vascular disease because it targets the clinically closest endpoint (incident peripheral artery disease; PAD is a core manifestation within peripheral vascular disease), comes from a disease-focused PAD study, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (~1.3M), and shows strong PRS signal via effect size (HR per SD 1.66, tight CI) with broad multi-ancestry evaluation and large validation (n=304,294). The main runner-up for exact label match is PGS002055 (peripheral vascular disease, unspecified), but it is a UKB portability-framework score with only a weak partial correlation (0.0175) and no effect-size/AUC evidence suggesting comparable discrimination; PGS001843 is similar but weaker partial-r. PGS005158 is restricted to PAD in type 2 diabetes, uses only 19 GWAS hits, has much weaker HR (1.13), and heavy clinical covariate packaging, making it less suitable as a general PVD PRS.

All candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported: malignant neoplasm of ovary), same publication family (Cancer PRSweb), same EUR-only ancestry context, same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same training/validation cohorts and sizes—so the decision should hinge on within-family performance and structural strength. PGS000550 (PRS-CS; ~1.1M variants) has the best reported discrimination among the set (full-model AUROC 0.568 vs 0.567/0.558/0.556/0.552) and the strongest effect-size signal (OR per SD 1.286 vs 1.263 for PGS000549 and lower for others), with the highest Nagelkerke R² (0.0113). Compared to the strongest runner-up PGS000549 (GWAS hits; 16 variants), PGS000550’s genome-wide shrinkage construction and materially larger variant set align with better expected PRS capture of polygenic signal, while also showing slightly better observed metrics in the same evaluation setting.

All four candidates are near-clones: same prostate cancer endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all aligned), same publication family, same training cohort (UKB), same stated covariates (0), and same validation context/size and ancestry mix. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any, the best tie-break is within-family empirical performance plus the structural advantage of multi-score aggregation. PGS004155 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the highest full-model AUROC (0.7049 vs 0.7003/0.6994/0.6962) and highest R² (0.1280 vs 0.1213/0.1202/0.1154), and also the strongest effect size (OR 2.166 vs 2.109/2.112/2.077). Compared to the strongest runner-up PGS004139, PGS004155 shows a consistent edge across AUROC, R², and OR while also being an ensemble (MultiPRS), which is a positive structural signal when endpoints/covariates are otherwise identical.

PGS000922 is the best direct-match to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both sarcoidosis) and provides clean PRS-only performance metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.6428; PGS R2 no covariates=0.0174) with only basic covariates, staying well below the heritability ceiling. The main runner-up is PGS000923, which has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R2 but is explicitly a time-to-event endpoint (TTE sarcoidosis), a mild endpoint mismatch for generic sarcoidosis risk; given the small metric gap and the upstream prior ranking, the non-TTE direct diagnosis model is preferred. PGS001872 and PGS002084 are weaker due to trait_efo mapping to skin sarcoidosis and lacking PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only partial-r), making them less directly supported for the generic sarcoidosis target.

PGS004163 is the strongest direct-match within the coherent 2023 Am J Hum Genet five-biobank RA cluster: same endpoint framing (Seropositive RA), same covariate handling (covariates=0), same training/validation context and ancestries as its siblings, but it has the best reported discrimination/effect-size among them (full-model AUROC 0.7469 and R² 0.1376; OR per SD 2.46) versus the closest runner-up PGS004049 (AUROC 0.7283, R² 0.1220; OR 2.37). PGS001311, while reporting clean PGS-only AUROC/R², comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework with only 3 variants and a time-to-event endpoint, which is a weaker archetype for external benchmark performance compared with the disease-focused multi-method biobank evaluation family; its PRS-only R² (0.0585) is also notably lower than the RA-cluster’s reported R² values.

PGS001280 is the best direct-match for pulmonary embolism among the shortlist because it targets PE specifically (trait_efo pulmonary embolism; phenotyping_reported TTE PE) and, unlike PGS003861, reports clean PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.60765; PGS-only R2=0.01403) with basic covariates and a large UKB development set. The top-ranked PGS003861 has exact PE labeling and is disease-focused in Han Chinese, but only provides a full-model AUROC (0.765) with unknown covariates and no PRS-only AUC/R2, making its apparent discrimination likely non-comparable for PRS benchmarking. Compared with the closest runner-up PGS001277, PGS001280 has tighter endpoint fidelity (PE alone vs PE +/- DVT) while having very similar study family and evaluation context; although PGS001277 has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R2, the composite endpoint mismatch makes it a weaker direct match for PE.

All three candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), ancestry (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), cohorts (MGI), covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and validation size (n=5,500), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2. In this same-study, same-endpoint setting, the best-supported choice is the sibling with the strongest observed discrimination/effect-size package: PGS000471 has higher full-model AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557 for PGS000470 and 0.524 for PGS000469), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154 vs 0.00141), and stronger risk stratification (OR top 1% vs rest 3.77 vs 2.45 vs 1.48) and per-SD OR (1.401 vs 1.308 vs 1.09). Thus PGS000471 has a clear multi-metric advantage over the strongest runner-up (PGS000470) within an otherwise comparable context.

Both candidates map to the same disease concept (trait_efo=psoriatic arthritis), but PGS001287 has substantially stronger and cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.67648 and PGS-only R2=0.0335 (with basic covariates listed separately), and these are plausible under the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0735). It is also trained at large scale (n=269,704) and has a large European validation record (n=24,905). In contrast, PGS000342 is a very small 11-variant GWAS-hit/HLA score with only a low full-model AUROC=0.562 (no PGS-only metrics) in a much smaller validation (n=543) and unknown covariates, making its PRS strength hard to assess and likely weaker. The main drawback for PGS001287 is its pan-trait UK Biobank framework origin, which lowers confidence, but the multi-field advantage in PRS-only metrics and scale over PGS000342 is clear.

PGS005219 is the strongest direct-match OSA score in the shortlist: it is disease-focused (OSA), built with a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CSs) at ~983k variants and developed across multiple major cohorts (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP) with multi-ancestry evaluation. While no candidate reports clean PGS-only AUC/R2, PGS005219 shows markedly stronger PRS signal than its closest sibling PGS005220 via a higher per-SD effect size (OR 1.98 vs 1.53) under otherwise near-identical design (same paper, covariates, validation size, and full-model AUROC 0.79). It also has a stronger evidence package than the MVP GWAS-hits scores (PGS003857/PGS003858; sparse 18/6 variants, lower full-model AUROC ~0.77) and clearly outperforms the ExPRSweb framework score PGS003213 (full-model AUROC 0.527, weaker OR 1.106).

PGS001137 is the strongest direct match with the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it targets retinal detachment with matching phenotyping_reported, and it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.573 and PGS-only R²=0.00663 (both below the local h2_obs ceiling ~0.0042–0.0049 in scale-consistent magnitude, i.e., not implausibly inflated). The closest runner-up is PGS002040 (same UKB portability study family and similar endpoint wording), but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² and only provides partial-r=0.0276, which is less directly comparable and not clearly stronger than PGS001137’s PRS-only metrics. PGS000990 is from the same snpnet framework paper but uses a time-to-event ‘detachments and breaks’ endpoint and has materially weaker PRS-only performance (AUROC=0.542, R²=0.00213). PGS001833 also trails PGS002040 on partial-r (0.0218 vs 0.0276).

All candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder carcinoma in EUR and none report PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on within-family comparability and effect-size/performance proxies. PGS000613 (Cancer PRSweb, UKB-derived) has the strongest overall signal among the near-clone PRSweb siblings: it shows higher full-model AUROC (0.571 vs 0.567 for PGS000611) and stronger effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.301; top 1% vs rest OR 2.91) than the closest runner-up PGS000611 (OR per SD 1.284; top 1% OR 2.66), with identical covariates and validation context (n=13,530). While PGS000723 has a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.583) and huge validation N, it lacks training/sample details and effect-size metrics and uses a different minimal covariate specification, making that AUROC less interpretable/comparable; thus the better-supported, internally consistent PRSweb P+T score PGS000613 is preferred.

All candidates are direct matches for thyroid carcinoma (trait_efo/phenotyping_reported both thyroid cancer) and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on within-family comparability of full-model metrics and effect sizes with similar basic covariates. Among the PRSweb siblings with identical covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), PGS000631 shows the strongest discrimination/proxy signals (highest full-model AUROC 0.636 and highest Nagelkerke R² 0.0478, plus strongest per-SD OR 1.651) compared with the closest runner-up PGS000630 (AUROC 0.626, R² 0.0393, OR 1.598). PGS000208 has a much higher AUROC (0.751) but it is a covariate-heavier package including family history, making that AUROC less comparable to a standalone PRS and therefore discounted despite large validation N.

All three are broadly on-target for pulmonary fibrosis, but PGS001791 and PGS004695 are the tighter endpoint match (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis). Between those, PGS001791 has materially stronger PRS construction and benchmarking evidence: a genome-wide PRS-CS-auto score (910,439 variants) from a large multi-biobank framework with a clean PRS-comparable metric reported (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out / PGS-only R2 = 0.005929) and basic covariates only. PGS004695 is a very sparse 23-SNP GWS score and reports only an HR (high vs low quintile) without PRS-only AUC/R2, and it is embedded in an exposure-focused incidence study with additional epidemiologic covariates, making it less directly comparable as a standalone PRS. PGS001030 has stronger PRS-only R2 (0.0142) but is a pan-trait UKB sparse-framework score with a broader/less specific phenotype (“pulmonary fibrosis” rather than idiopathic PF), which domain guidance suggests typically underperforms disease-focused/multi-cohort disease-endpoint scores when available; thus PGS001791 is the best-supported direct-match overall.

All top four candidates (PGS000136/133/134/135) are near-clones from the same schizophrenia-focused Am J Psychiatry study with identical endpoint fidelity (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both schizophrenia) and similarly basic covariates, so the main differentiators are the within-family performance/effect-size signals. PGS000136 has the strongest combined evidence: the highest reported AUROC among the multi-record siblings (full_model_auc 0.64 vs 0.60 for PGS000133/PGS000134) and a strong per-SD OR (~1.7), indicating meaningful PRS signal. Although PGS000135 reports a higher AUROC (0.74), it is supported by only a single record with much smaller validation n (9,569) and no effect-size reported, making that apparent edge less well-supported than PGS000136’s more corroborated performance plus effect-size evidence. PGS002785 is not a direct endpoint match (phenotyping_reported is cognitive function) and its partial R² is not comparable for schizophrenia risk prediction.

All candidates are direct matches for squamous cell carcinoma with EUR-only evaluation and no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so we rely on within-family comparability and effect-size/performance proxies. Among the tightly comparable Cancer PRSweb siblings (PGS000461/PGS000465/PGS000463: same publication, same training cohort MGI, same basic covariates age/sex/batch/PCs, same validation n=8,473), PGS000461 has the best full-model AUROC (0.599 vs 0.593 and 0.589) and the highest Nagelkerke R² (0.0304 vs 0.0268 and 0.0282), with a slightly stronger per-SD OR (1.491 vs 1.448/1.457). PGS000731 has a marginally higher AUROC (0.605) and larger validation n, but has unknown covariates and lacks training sample details, making its AUROC less interpretable versus the clean, near-clone PRSweb comparison set. Therefore PGS000461 is the best-supported choice over the strongest runner-up PGS000731.

PGS003381 is the strongest direct-match for the target (uterine cancer) because its endpoint is the clinically dominant subtype (endometrial carcinoma) with coherent phenotype fields, and it shows substantially stronger reported discrimination in the selected European validation (full-model AUROC 0.761, R² 0.11 with only basic covariates: age + PCs) than the closest runner-up PGS001795 (uterine cancer) whose PRS-comparable signal is extremely small (PGS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R²=0.001948; full-model AUROC 0.66). The older PRSweb uterus scores (PGS000541/PGS000542) have much weaker AUROC (~0.57) and sparse variant sets, and PGS003740 lacks comparable performance metrics and has very small training/validation. While PGS003381 lacks explicit PRS-only AUC/R², its much stronger overall performance proxy with clean covariates and high-fidelity dominant-subtype endpoint outweighs the framework-style, low-R² evidence in PGS001795.

PGS000024 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused T1D score in this shortlist: it targets the exact trait (trait_efo/type 1 diabetes mellitus; phenotyping_reported Type 1 diabetes), comes from a dedicated T1D genetic risk score paper, uses a richer variant set (85 SNPs with interaction modelling) than the other disease-focused GWAS-hit scores (PGS000023: 7 SNPs; PGS000022: 37 SNPs), and shows the best reported discrimination signal among the disease-focused candidates (full-model AUROC 0.921 vs 0.8508 and 0.817). The main runner-up is PGS001297 because it reports clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.771, R2 0.0912), but it is a pan-trait UK Biobank framework score (“across 813 traits”) that domain guidance flags as less reliable for external performance than disease-focused models when a strong disease-specific alternative exists. PGS004874 is also framework-like and incident/time-to-event packaged (C-index 0.77) with unclear training (n=404, 1000G), so it is less directly comparable as a standalone T1D PRS despite large evaluation N.

PGS001536 is the only shortlist candidate with clean PRS-only performance reported for vitiligo (PGS-only AUROC=0.64193; PGS-only R2=0.01621), with basic covariates and a large training/validation setting (UKB; train n=269,704; eval n=67,425). Its PRS-only R2 is well below the vitiligo h2 ceiling (h2_obs~0.17), so the metric looks plausible. The main runner-up by trait label is PGS000738, but it has an endpoint-fidelity red flag (phenotyping_reported='Red hair') and only a pseudo-R2/full-model R2 without PRS-only discrimination, making it less directly supported as a vitiligo PRS. PGS000760 has a clear endpoint mismatch (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients) and lacks PRS-comparable metrics, so it is not competitive despite an HR being reported.

All candidates are direct ulcerative colitis matches by trait_efo/phenotyping, but PGS004253 is the only clearly disease-focused UC PRS in the shortlist (Nat Commun paper specifically on UC prediction in an immune-checkpoint-inhibitor colitis context) and it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.84, 95% CI 1.76–1.93), which is a strong proxy for PRS discrimination. The strongest runner-up is PGS001307 (snpnet UKB framework), which has clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 (PGS-only AUROC=0.638, R2=0.0238) but comes from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework that domain guidance flags as less reliable for external benchmark performance; its PRS-only R2 is also modest. PGS004253’s full-model AUROC (0.66) is not treated as PRS-only, but combined with the much stronger OR and non-framework study archetype, it has the clearer overall evidence package than the UKB framework alternatives (PGS001306/PGS001307) and the portability-paper scores with weaker/less interpretable metrics (PGS001855/PGS002066).

All candidates are broadly endpoint-aligned to urolithiasis, but the strongest head-to-head is within the same publication family (the UKB portability paper): PGS002075 (LDpred2, genome-wide 731,196 variants) vs PGS001864 (penalized regression, 5,599 variants). With identical phenotype/covariates and similar training/validation context, PGS002075 shows higher PRS signal in the selected European validation (partial-r 0.0385 vs 0.0323) and has a materially more genome-wide construction, which is a positive structural signal for polygenic disease prediction. The alternative with explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 (PGS001250) comes from the sparse pan-trait UKB framework and uses a time-to-event endpoint, and its PRS-only AUROC is modest (0.5668), so it does not clearly outweigh the better-supported portability-family genome-wide score. The 2024 risk-factor-integration scores (PGS004563/PGS004493) lack comparable discrimination metrics and have only moderate ORs (~1.23–1.28), so they provide weaker benchmark-transfer evidence than the portability-family winner.

All candidates are direct matches to type 2 diabetes, but PGS002308 has the strongest overall evidence package for a standalone T2D PRS: it is explicitly a disease-focused trans-ancestry PRS (PRS-CSx) with broad multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/GME) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.96, tight CI), suggesting robust PRS signal. The main runner-up is PGS001781, which shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.852) and large validation N, but it comes from a risk-factor integration study and the very high AUROC is likely more covariate-driven (and its PRS effect size is notably weaker, OR=1.52). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any candidate, the stronger PRS effect size plus explicit trans-ancestry design and diverse evaluation make PGS002308 the best-supported choice.
